answer: Because the knoll ordering is published with the copper batch, the vault audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 25% of the queue is processed in arrival order. A farm that floods the queue early hence gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. A 156 account operation therefore ties up 32 million dollars of idle capital. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
